title.en: A Spring River on a Night of Flowers and Moonlight

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource; the variant readings it marks are left out. Lines broken at the punctuation for reading; text unchanged.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，删去其所注异文。按标点分行，文字未改。

basis.en: Tang dynasty poem; the author died around 720.
basis.zh: 唐诗，作者约卒于 720 年。

note.en: Only two poems by Zhang Ruoxu survive, and this one was little noticed for centuries before later critics placed it at the summit of Tang poetry; the Qing scholar Wang Kaiyun said that with a single poem he stood among the masters. It follows one night, from moonrise over the tide to moonset in the sea mist, and in the middle asks the question this library keeps asking. Notice that the rhyme changes every four lines, as the moon keeps moving across the sky.
note.zh: 张若虚的诗只传下两首，这一首沉寂了几百年，才被后人推到唐诗的顶峰；清人王闿运评它“孤篇横绝，竟为大家”。全诗写一夜，从月出潮生写到月落海雾，中段提出了这座图书馆一直在问的问题。留意它每四句换一次韵，就像月亮一直在天上移动。

pick.en: I return to this poem for its middle: who on this bank first saw the moon, and in what year did the moon first shine on a person? Human lives go on generation after generation, the moon looks the same each year, and the poem does not find that sad; it finds it continuous. A library is built on the same arithmetic: each reader is brief, and the reading is long.
pick.zh: 我常回到这首诗的中段：江畔何人初见月？江月何年初照人？人生代代无穷已，江月年年望相似，诗人并不为此伤感，而是从中看见一种延续。图书馆也建立在同样的算术上：每个读者都短暂，而阅读很长。

excerpt.orig: 江畔何人初見月，江月何年初照人？
excerpt.en: Who on this riverbank first saw the moon? / In what year did the river moon first shine on a person?
excerpt.zh: 江畔何人初见月，江月何年初照人？

gloss.en: Shimmering: moonlight rippling on the water.
The ancients thought frost fell from the sky like snow. Here the ‘flowing frost’ is the moonlight itself.
gloss.zh: 古人以为霜和雪一样从空中落下，这里以“流霜”比喻月光。

gloss.en: Green Maple Bank, a place name (there is one near Liuyang in Hunan), used here for any place of parting.
gloss.zh: 青枫浦：地名，今湖南浏阳境内有青枫浦，这里泛指离别之地。

gloss.en: The stone on which cloth was beaten clean. Women beating clothes in the moonlight is a stock image of wives missing men far away.
gloss.zh: 捣衣砧：捣衣用的垫石。月下捣衣，是古诗中思妇怀远的常见意象。

gloss.en: Wild geese, like the fish of the next line, were said to carry letters. Here they fly on and cannot carry even the light.
gloss.zh: 古有鸿雁传书、鱼传尺素之说。鸿雁长飞，也带不走月光，音信难通。

gloss.en: Jieshi on the northern coast and the Xiao and Xiang rivers in the far south: the whole breadth of the land between parted people.
gloss.zh: 碣石在北方海边，潇湘在南方，泛指天南地北。

marginalia.en: Of the five words in the title, 月 appears fifteen times in the poem’s 252 characters and 江 twelve, while 花 and 夜 appear only twice each. The poem is mostly river and moon, turned again and again in a changing light.
marginalia.zh: 题目五个字里，“月”在全诗二百五十二字中出现了十五次，“江”十二次，“花”和“夜”各只有两次。这首诗大半是江与月，在变化的光里一再翻转。

marginalia.en: Here the poem turns from the river and the moon to two people: a traveller in a boat and a woman in a moonlit tower. From this stanza on, the moonlight is the distance between them.
marginalia.zh: 诗在这里从江月转向两个人：扁舟上的游子，明月楼上的思妇。从这一章起，月光就是他们之间的距离。
